history.summary: Chandika Sthan is the prominent Shakti shrine of Munger: a Siddhi-Peetha and one of the 51 Shakta pithas, located about 2 km northeast of Munger town on the Ganga bank (address given as Biratpur/Basudevpur, Munger-811201). Puranic tradition holds that Sati's left eye fell here when Shiva wandered with her corpse, and the shrine is famous in local belief for curing eye ailments. The main temple sits inside a small natural cave - locally called 'Karna's Kadai' (an inverted-vessel-like cave). Legend also calls the goddess Vikrama Chandi, after King Vikrama, her ardent devotee. Murtis of various forms of Goddess Shakti are worshipped in the complex. No published source documents the founding date or dynasty of this shrine (verify). CSV ERROR FLAG: the CSV 'state' column held the town name (Munger); the real state is Bihar. Town note: sources place the shrine at Biratpur/Basudevpur just outside Munger town; the CSV town 'Munger' is correct at town level. Opening hours are not published - verify on site.

town_description: Munger is an ancient city in eastern Bihar on the south bank of the Ganges, once the capital of the Anga kingdom and later of Mir Qasim; the Munger Fort and the Ganga-side Yoga Vidya campus (Karna Chaura) anchor its identity as a seat of both history and yoga. It lies about 175 km east of Patna.
